text:
Stay silent and alone:

almost everything is excess and needless.

From the branch hangs the fruit

and from the pedicel the rose,

not only for the purposes of desire,

but for the inert blindness

that vision exaggerates

in reach and in meaning;

and what you sing asleep

is your true song.


Stay alone and silent:

almost everything is needless and excess.

No expense is recovered,

nor is the exchanged gold worth

the coin you have paid

for heaps of fleece.

For by thefts the heart gives

the beats you make use of,

and though you imagine you pay,

you owe it to the pantheon.

translation.title: Stay Silent
translation.editorial_note: The translation keeps the moral aphorism and the reversal of needless excess.
